page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-56 is a compute-focused server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture. It features 56 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped to 28 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The system is equipped with 224 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local NVMe storage or integrated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage.

Benchmark evaluations place this instance in the top tier for memory performance and text generation speed on small language models. It demonstrates strong multi-core capabilities, ranking in the top 25% for stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, Geekbench multi-core scores, and Passmark CPU physics tests. Cryptographic operations and database tasks are highly efficient, as evidenced by strong performance in Passmark CPU encryption and Redis SET operations, which exceed 61 million operations per second. Single-core performance and large-block memory bandwidth remain in the average tier.

Given its high physical core density and dedicated AMD EPYC compute resources, the c2d-standard-56 offers high resource density for multi-threaded workloads without the overhead of GPU accelerators. The absence of bundled local storage means storage costs are decoupled, allowing for custom network storage provisioning. This profile is highly suited for compute-heavy tasks such as software compilation, ray tracing, image processing, and multi-threaded database operations.
